title.title: The Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
title.subtitle: Claim: on every CM abelian variety, every rational $(p,p)$ class comes from algebraic cycles

plain: Every 'shadow' that looks cast by a real curve or surface really is, on the most symmetric shapes

nodes.label: Theorem 1.1: every CM Hodge class is algebraic
a ball-quotient surface with a nonzero period

beats.text: Theorem 1.1: the cycle class map hits every rational $(p,p)$ class
Every CM Hodge class reduces to one line on a product of four CM varieties
A surface mapping to all four, with a nonzero period, gives the cycle

steps: Reduce every such class to one basic four-piece pattern
Map a single surface into all four pieces at once
A nonzero integral over it makes its image the needed cycle

boxes: a surface mapped to all four

achievement.label: Hodge conjecture (Hodge 1950), the CM abelian case
achievement.context: Before: Deligne (1982) made the classes absolute Hodge; Markman (2025) settled all abelian fourfolds
achievement.note: A special case of Hodge, not the Millennium problem; it implies Tate over $\mathbb{F}_q$

voice.text: On these symmetric shapes, every class that looks algebraic comes from real cycles.
Reduce everything to one four-piece pattern, then build it from a single surface.
Claimed: Hodge holds for every CM abelian variety.
